full_judgment:
SM Emdadul Hoque, J: This First Appeal at the instance of the appellant Janata Bank Limited, represented by its Deputy General-Manager, Barisal Corporate Branch, Barisal is directed against the impugned judgment and decree dated 17-9-2017 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court and Artha Rin Adalat, Barisal, in Artha Rin Suit No. 8 of 2015 dismissing the suit. 

 2. Facts necessary for disposal of the appeal, in short, is that the present appellant Janata Bank Limited, represented by its Deputy General-Manager, Janata bank Limited, Barisal Corporate Branch, Barisal as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 8 of 2015 against the respondent for a decree for the outstanding amount of Taka 69,73,238 along with 12% interest from 25-5-2015 to till realization of the decreetal amount stating inter-alia that the defendant-respondent No.1 is the proprietor of M/s Mandi Enterprize of and the respondent No.2 is the grantor. The defendant No. 1 filed an application for loan on 15-9-2010 and accordingly the loan was approved through Janata Bank letter No. জিএম/সিসি(হা./১৯০২(ক)/২০১০-এ আর dated 16-9-2010 with 13% interest. On an application of the defendant No.1 dated 15-9-2010 the appellant bank sanctioned the loan amounting to Taka 14,00,000 with 13% interest and accordingly the defendant-respondent No.1 signing all the documents and took loan through mortgaged deed No. 8603 dated 21-9-2010 and accordingly the respondent No. 1 withdrawn the said amount of loan and thereafter the said loan was rescheduled on 14-12-2011 with 15% interest subject to payment of the amount within 15-9-2012 and accordingly the defendant No. 1 also signed all the charge documents and others to obtain the loan. But the said loanee subsequently failed to pay the outstanding loan amount of the Bank. Thereafter, the Bank issued legal notice on 14-8-2013 to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 but no respond. 

 8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat the plaintiff-bank preferred this First Appeal. 

 10. Mr Md Nazmul Hoque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that the court below passed the impugned judgment without following the procedure of law which is miscarriage of justice and, as such, the same is liable to be sat-aside. The main contention of the learned Advocate is that though the matter was fixed for ex-parte hearing but the Artha Rin Adalat without following the provision of section 6(4) and section 19(6) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 passed the impugned judgment which the impugned judgment and decree should liable to be sat-aside. The another ground of the learned Advocate is that as per provision of section 2(8) and section 4 of the Banker's Book Evidence Act, 1891, the Act No. XVIII of 1891 a certified copy of any entry in a Banker's Book shall in all legal proceeding be admissible in evidence but the trial court did not consider the said provision of law and illegally passed the impugned judgment and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree should liable to be dismissed. He further submits that though it is the duty of the appellant-bank to examine the witnesses but unfortunately the learned Advocate did not file any application for adjournment of the ex-parte hearing and, as such, the trial court passed the impugned judgment and by the impugned judgment the plaintiff-bank face irreparable loss and injury if the matter should not be consider on the basis of the documents since the defendant did not appear to contest the suit. At the time of hearing of the appeal the learned Advocate produced all the original documents regarding the loan. Thus he prayed for allowing the appeal. 

 12. We have heard the learned Advocate of the appellant, perused the impugned judgment and decree, the plaint and the photocopies of the documents of the loan which all filed before the trial court through freshti form by the plaintiff side at the time of filing of the suit. We have also examined the original documents which has been brought before this court by the learned Advocate. 

 14. It appears that the plaintiff side tried to auction sale the mortgage property and accordingly which was published in the daily "Amader Somoy" under section 12 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. It also appears from the statements of the plaint that after legal notice the defendant side paid Taka 3,00,000 of the loan money but thereafter keep silent and thus the plaintiff side filed the suit for realization of lone money of Taka 69,73,238 with 12% interest till realization of the decreetal amount. 

 29. In the result, the appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and decree dated 17-9-2017 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court and Artha Rin Adalat, Barisal, in Artha Rin Suit No. 8 of 2015 is hereby set-aside.
